[[def-cm14-involution]] and [[def-cm14-complete-integrability]] define the
model properties and the datum. Two features are essential and logically
separate: the members of the datum must be in involution, and their
differentials must be independent on the regular locus; neither condition
implies the other. The striking conclusions are conditional on strictly
more than involution and independence:
[[pthm-cm14-regular-tori]] requires a regular value with nonempty compact
connected fibre and a saturated neighbourhood on which the integral map
is a proper submersion with connected fibres, and it consumes the Axiom
of Countable Choice through the published lattice lemma, as its statement
records; [[pthm-cm14-action-angle]] additionally produces the period-one
action-angle coordinates of [[def-action-and-angle-coordinates]] and the
linear Hamiltonian motion on the tori, under the same hypotheses;
identification with Cartesian model motions additionally uses $d\equiv0$; for a generalized-coordinate immersion the Hamiltonian curves correspond to the substituted Lagrange equations, and identifying them with ambient motions requires the additional reconstruction hypotheses. Compactness cannot
be dropped (a free-particle regular level is a noncompact manifold, not a
torus), regularity cannot be dropped (the zero level of the isotropic
oscillator is a point), and the conclusions are local over a ball of
regular values — no global product structure or single-valued global
action-angle chart is asserted.

The angles of [[def-action-and-angle-coordinates]] and of
[[pthm-cm14-action-angle]] are period-one, with
$\omega=\sum_{i}d\theta_{i}\wedge dI_{i}$ and action coordinates of
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; the numbers
$\partial h/\partial I_{i}$ are then frequencies in cycles per unit time,
not angular rates. The radian convention is recovered by the explicit
rescaling $\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}=2\pi\theta$,
$I^{\mathrm{rad}}=I/(2\pi)$ of [[cor-cm-action-angle-radian-scaling]],
under which the form is unchanged and the angular rates are twice
$\pi$ times the cyclic frequencies; the two conventions are never mixed
in this page. The sources use the radian action $J=\frac1{2\pi}\oint
p\,dq$; the period-one action of a mechanical one-degree-of-freedom model
is its $2\pi$-multiple, a convention recorded in the companion examples.

vectors $e_1,e_2$ perpendicular to the common incoming direction $\hat u$.

$P=b e_\varphi-\sqrt{a^2-b^2}\,\hat u$. The transverse component of the
reflected direction is a positive multiple of $e_\varphi$, so its outgoing
azimuth is $\varphi$. Let $D=(0,a)\times(0,2\pi)$ and
$Y=(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)$. Adopt uniform incident area measure
$\nu(B)=\int_B b\,d\lambda_2(b,\varphi)$ on Borel subsets of $D$ and
solid-angle measure $\Omega(B)=\int_B\sin\theta\,d\lambda_2(\theta,\varphi)$

[[def-cm-scattering-data]]. Define the **contact cross-section measure**
by $\sigma(B):=\nu(T^{-1}(B))$, where
$T(b,\varphi)=(\theta(b),\varphi)$ is the outgoing direction map.
For an angular band $A\subseteq(0,\pi)$ abbreviate
$\sigma(A):=\sigma(A\times(0,2\pi))$.

$\sigma(B)=\int_B f\,d\Omega$ for every Borel $B\subseteq Y$.
This is a local definition for the fixed-wall contact model, independent
of the smooth central-model class of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]].

supply no atoms; free incoming lines with $b>a$ do not hit the sphere and
are excluded from this contact cross-section.

inherited from the statement of
[[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]], whose distributional jump
lemma uses it; the algebraic clauses used here do not otherwise use choice.
Adopt the impact and open-mass extensions of [[post-cm15-impulse]], with
$m_1,m_2>0$, an interval $I$ with nonempty interior, $t_*\in\operatorname{int} I$, an impulse motion
$x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ run in the isolated reciprocal impulse model at $t_*$
with impulse $J$ and one-sided velocities $v_i^\pm$, and write
$$M:=m_1+m_2,\qquad \mu:=\frac{m_1m_2}{M},\qquad P(t):=m_1x_1'(t)+m_2x_2'(t)\qquad(t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}).$$
Only the one-sided limits of $P$ at $t_*$ are used; no derivative of the
position curves at the contact time is assumed.
Then:

1. **(Momentum continuity.)** The total momentum is continuous across the
   impact,
   $$P(t_*^+)=P(t_*^-),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^2 m_i\bigl(v_i^+-v_i^-\bigr)=0,$$
   and the impulse delivered to label $1$ is removed from label $2$:
   $J=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=-m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)$.
2. **(Smooth-force exclusion.)** Suppose this same candidate motion $x$ from
   clause 1 also satisfies the smooth force branch of
   [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] on $I$,
   with the force maps continuous there. Then the momentum curves
   $p_i=m_ix_i'$ are of class $C^1$ on $I$; in particular
   $$p_i(t_*^+)=p_i(t_*^-)\qquad(i=1,2).$$
   Clause 1 identifies the jump of $p_1$ with the same impulse $J$, so
   $J=0$: no candidate motion carrying a nonzero isolated impulse can also
   be a motion of that smooth-force class. The finite-jump model of
   [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (i) is therefore a genuine extension of the
   smooth-force branch, not one of its cases.
3. **(Collinear restitution solution.)** Suppose in addition that the
   contact is collinear with contact direction $n$ and coefficient of
   restitution $e\in[0,1]$ ([[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii)). Then
   $$J=\mu(1+e)\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),$$
   $J$ is parallel to $n$, the centre-of-mass velocity
   $V:=M^{-1}(m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-)$ is unchanged across the impact, and the
   post-impact velocities are
   $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$
4. **(Kinetic energy of the impact.)** The kinetic-energy change across the
   impact is
   $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2} -\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2} =-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0,$$
   with equality if and only if $e=1$ or $v_2^-=v_1^-$. For $0\le e<1$ the
   contact model is dissipative: the total kinetic energy of the two labels
   is not conserved across the impact, and the deficit
   $\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ is a quantity of the
   adopted contact law. This item identifies it with no measured heat,
   temperature, sound or deformation observable.
5. **(Momentum balance alone does not determine the impact.)** In the
   collinear case with $d^-:=v_2^--v_1^-$ and $d_n:=\langle d^-,n\rangle<0$,
   the impulse equations of clause 1 alone leave the scalar impulse magnitude
   free: for every real $J_n$ with $J_n\le \mu d_n$ (so that the contact is
   separating or grazing) the velocities
   $$v_1^+=v_1^-+\frac{J_n}{m_1}n,\qquad v_2^+=v_2^--\frac{J_n}{m_2}n$$
   satisfy the reciprocal impulse equations with impulse $J=J_nn$ and
   preserve the total momentum, and their kinetic-energy change is
   $$\Delta K(J_n)=-J_n\,d_n+\frac{J_n^2}{2\mu},$$
   whose minimum over the admissible range is
   $\Delta K(\mu d_n)=-\frac{\mu}{2}d_n^2$ at the perfectly inelastic value
   $J_n=\mu d_n$ (that is, $e=0$). The value of
   $J_n$ is fixed only by the contact law of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (ii), which selects $J_n=\mu(1+e)d_n$; in particular momentum balance
   alone does not determine the post-impact velocities.
6. **(Open-body and rocket laws.)** Under [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause
   (iii), with differentiable $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ and $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$,
   $F:I\to\mathbb R^3$, $r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to[0,\infty)$,
   and $w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the
   material balance identities, one has on $I$
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v\bigr).$$
   In particular: (a) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ then
   $m\,v'=F$ and $(mv)'=F$; (b) if $r_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ and
   $r_{\mathrm{out}}=-m'>0$ (mass loss) then
   $$m\,v'=F+r_{\mathrm{out}}\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr)=F-m'\bigl(v-w_{\mathrm{out}}\bigr),$$
   so the **thrust** is $T:=r_{\mathrm{out}}(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})=-m'(v-w_{\mathrm{out}})$,
   and the closed-system law $(mv)'=F$ fails unless
   $w_{\mathrm{out}}=0$; (c) if $r_{\mathrm{out}}=0$ and $w_{\mathrm{in}}=0$
   then $m\,v'=F-r_{\mathrm{in}}v$: capture contributes the acceleration
   $-(r_{\mathrm{in}}/m)v$, opposing $v$, while $(mv)'=F$ still holds.

laws and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the Galilean translations and
boosts of the model's frame class. All of this is conditional on P1, P2, P4,
P5 and P6 and on the cited mathematical suppliers; none of it is a statement
that any physical system is exactly described by the model.

[[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]], which reads a
time-dependent coordinate map $X$ with invertible $X_{q}$ into the transport
identity $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=X_{q}^{\mathsf T}E_{L}(x)$; this is a local
coordinate change, and it is a global chart only when it is also one-to-one.
Thus the model equation takes the form of the Euler-Lagrange equation of the
substituted Lagrangian in each such coordinate description, and
[[pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge]], which records that adding the total time
derivative of a $C^{3}$ function on the full time-configuration domain with
action dimension changes the action by endpoint values only, that changing the
potential representative $U\mapsto U+c(t)$ is an instance of this, and that
nonzero dimensionless rescaling of the Lagrangian leaves the stationary curves
unchanged.
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] collects the
generalized-coordinate dictionary — the immersion $X$, the substituted
Lagrangian with kinetic metric $G=DX^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX$, generalized
forces $Q=DX^{\mathsf T}f$ and the declared Lagrange equations with residual
generalized force. Full-dimensional nonsingular maps give local coordinates;
constraint parametrizations cover the full constrained locus and may have
multiple coordinate representatives. The purely mathematical
[[lem-cm07-immersion-euler-lagrange-transport]] proves the transport identity
for non-square immersions.
[[pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-constraints]] then proves the
constraint-elimination theorem for the scleronomic ideal branch: on a
surjective immersed parametrization $X(\Omega)=\mathcal C\cap Q$, a coordinate
curve solves the Lagrange equations of the substituted Lagrangian exactly when the induced configuration
curve is a constrained motion of the model with its unique ideal reaction, so
the reaction never appears in the reduced equations. The page closes with

the mechanical branch is regular while singular velocity Hessians are
excluded, an unrestricted action principle is not generally equivalent to
d'Alembert dynamics for velocity constraints, and the whole reformulation is a
conditional theorem of the model, not empirical evidence.

The second half of the page marks the impact and open-flow boundaries.
[[post-cm15-impulse]] adopts three extensions of the force branch: an isolated
reciprocal impulse (equal and opposite finite momentum jumps at one time, the
regular dynamics retained away from it), a collinear restitution contact law
with coefficient $0\le e\le1$, and an open-body material accounting for matter
entering and leaving a body at given rates with given inertial velocities.
[[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]] proves the conditional consequences: the total
momentum is continuous across the impulse; a motion of the smooth-force branch
with continuous forces cannot carry a nonzero impulse, so the jump is a genuine
model extension; the collinear contact has the restitution velocities and the
kinetic-energy change $-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$, is
dissipative for $e<1$ and identifies the deficit with no measured quantity;
momentum balance alone leaves a one-parameter family of outcomes, so the
contact law is an independent datum; and the open-body accounting yields
$mv'=F+r_{\mathrm{in}}(w_{\mathrm{in}}-v)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$
with the rocket thrust as the special case.

localises its material balances to the field equations, and derives the
moving-control-region mass and momentum rates with the boundary speed $w$ and
the relative-velocity flux; it records the material and fixed special cases and
decomposes the boundary flux into inlet and outlet rates with flux-averaged
inertial velocities, reproducing the lumped open-body law of the impact
postulate. The closing remark [[rem-cm15-model-boundaries]] records what the
page does not claim: no monotonicity or completeness of the deflection map, no

scattering as a smooth-potential theorem, no measured values and no
electromagnetic identification, no individual-label angular distribution
without applying the two-label reconstruction in a specified inertial chart,

$h_{ab}=X_{ab}\cos(k\cdot x)+Y_{ab}\sin(k\cdot x)$, the momentum-space
harmonic-gauge condition $k^a\bar X_{ab}=k^a\bar Y_{ab}=0$, and the
linearized field equation
$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)+\Lambda h_{ab}=S_{ab}$. The elementary properties of the
phase coordinate — $n$ is null, every profile is annihilated by the flat
d'Alembertian and is constant along the null transport direction — are
proved in [[lem-gr-null-phase-coordinate]]. The SI coordinate-speed and
angular-frequency readings are stated in [[pthm-gr-plane-wave-polarizations]].
The observer screen, the screen and
spatial projectors $p$ and $h$ and the transverse-traceless projection
$\Pi_{n,s}$ are defined in [[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]], and
[[lem-gr-tt-screen-projector]] proves that $p$ and $h$ are the orthogonal
projections of rank two and three, that $\Pi_{n,s}$ is the orthogonal
projection onto the two-dimensional TT space, and that the half-trace
subtraction belongs to the rank-two screen: the same formula with the
rank-three projector is not trace-free.

downstream_pages.affected_use:
The companion page to [[qm-massive-particle-kinematics]] collects exact
worked computations, one distributional construction, one counterexample and
one conditional warning. [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-gaussian-position-momentum-packet]]
computes the normalized three-dimensional Gaussian packet of the spin-zero
massive model, shows that its momentum representative is again a normalized
Gaussian with width $\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$, and evaluates the model's
position and momentum outcome densities, their variances and the product
$\hbar/2$ in that family. [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-plane-wave-generalized-eigenfunction]]
defines the conjugate-linear Schwartz functional $u_{k}$ associated with the
formal plane wave, proves the generalized eigenrelation
$u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}u_{k}(\varphi)$, and proves that no $L^{2}$
class represents it, so the plane wave carries no state and no probability
density.
[[cex-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-cannot-hold-for-bounded-operators]] refutes the
existence of bounded operators satisfying $AB-BA=i\hbar I$, showing that the
canonical commutation relations require unbounded operators on a core, as
used by [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]].
[[texp-nrqm-kinematics-dirichlet-momentum-warning]] analyzes a hypothetical
confined-model extension and deduces that the formal interval momentum
$-i\hbar D$ on the Dirichlet domain is symmetric but not self-adjoint, that no
self-adjoint extension keeps the Dirichlet domain, and that the Dirichlet
functions are not momentum eigenfunctions of any such extension; the
framework's own momentum remains the full-line operator of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]. None of the items is
an experiment; no counts, calibration, resolution, efficiency, background,
uncertainty or data comparison appears, and no measured value of any model
parameter is asserted.

downstream_pages.affected_use:
This page develops the kinematic one-particle structure of the massive
spin-$s$ model that the kinematics postulate P5 assigns. The model reading is
fixed in [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]: the state
space is the component-valued Hilbert space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ of almost-everywhere classes,
read equivalently as the complete tensor product of the spatial factor with
the finite internal factor assigned in P6; position and momentum are the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ with their maximal domains and declared
units; the internal spin matrices act as matrix multiplications; and the
momentum representative and frame reading are fixed. The mathematics
supporting the definition is local to this page:
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]] proves
self-adjointness and norms for finite orthogonal sums,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
identifies the direct-sum and tensor descriptions,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] proves that the
componentwise operators are self-adjoint with their maximal domains, gives the
Fourier representation and the translation identities, and identifies the
coordinate translation groups with the spectral flows of the momentum
components, [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] proves
the canonical commutation relations on the Schwartz core, determines the
spectral projection-valued measures of $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ and shows that the
spatial measures commute with the internal factor, and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] constructs the unitary
momentum representation and its operator transforms.

downstream_pages.affected_use:
On this basis [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] proves the
equivalence of flow commutation, spectral commutation and domain invariance,
and derives the conservation of the outcome law and of the moments of a
self-adjoint observable from these hypotheses, including the case of a
self-adjoint unitary symmetry.
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
conjugates the bounded-potential operator by the translations, proves that a
translation is a symmetry exactly for potentials invariant under it almost
everywhere, shows that invariance under every translation forces an
almost-everywhere constant potential, and derives momentum conservation for
that case. [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] proves the
analogous statements for rotations — with conservation of the generators
$L_{i}$ — and for parity, whose conservation is read through the self-adjoint
unitary clause of the conservation theorem.
[[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]] states the
prescribed-coupling assumption P5a with the admissible bounded-coefficient
potentials, its units, the field definitions and the gauge transformation of
potentials and state phase; and
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-gauge-covariance]] proves the conjugation identity
transporting the minimal-coupling operator to the gauge-transformed
potentials, the exact criterion under which the gauge multiplier is a symmetry
of the fixed declared dynamics, the global-phase case, and the unitary
equivalence of the transformed time-dependent model carrying the transported
propagator.
[[rem-nrqm-symmetries-scope-and-empirical-status]] records the conditional
status of all of these statements, the empirical status of the model
parameters and of any symmetry identification for a laboratory system, the
excluded realizations and the supplier note on the operator development
consumed by the gauge items.

downstream_pages.affected_use:
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] defines the dimension-aware canonical maps of the
presentation by $C^{*}\omega_{2}=\omega_{1}$; a lower-dimensional map is a
symplectic immersion, while equal-dimensional maps have the matrix test
$DC^{\mathsf T}J\,DC=J$ and determinant consequence $|\det DC|=1$.
[[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]] proves that
the Hamiltonian evolution itself is canonical on its actual time-slice
domains — the two-form, the bracket and the determinant are preserved locally
in time, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time. Its time slices have the
$C^1$ regularity stated there; the separate fixed-map field-transport
theorem applies to an individual time slice only when it has additional
$C^2$ regularity.
[[pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canonical-maps]] proves that an
equal-dimensional local canonical transformation conjugates Hamiltonian
fields and transports the model's Hamiltonian systems and brackets.
[[pthm-cm13-liouville]] uses the phase-volume form
$\Omega=\omega^{\wedge n}/n!$ to prove conservation of phase volume: on its
actual domains the Hamiltonian evolution preserves the Lebesgue measure in
every full-dimensional canonical chart, under the stated Axiom of Countable
Choice used by the change-of-variables step. The phase-volume unit is action
to the power $3N$. [[pthm-cm13-generating-functions]] closes the
constructive part: first- and second-kind generating functions with
nondegenerate mixed derivative on nonempty admissible position and momentum domains generate canonical local diffeomorphisms of
the presentation, the local converse holds under an invertible
$(q,Q)$-projection, and a time-dependent generating function carries the
identity $p\cdot dq-H\,dt=P\cdot dQ-K\,dt+dS$ with $K=H+S_{t}$ and transports
Hamilton's equations between the two descriptions; the underlying calculus
of generating functions is that of [[cm-math-canonical]].

downstream_pages.affected_use:
This page is the Hamilton–Jacobi and integrability companion of
[[cm13-symplectic-geometry-and-canonical-methods]]. It adds no physical
assumption to the force branch: its definitions stipulate data and its theorems prove conditional statements
about a declared hyperregular potential presentation of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the momentum charts and
two-form of [[def-cm13-two-form]].
[[def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation]] fixes the Hamilton–Jacobi equation
associated with one of the presentation's momentum charts — the class of
$C^{3}$ action-dimension functions $S$ with
$S_{t}+H(t,q,S_{q})=0$ for the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] — and records that the equation is attached to
the declared chart, Legendre branch and potential representative.
[[def-cm14-complete-integral]] adds the no-caustic nondegeneracy
$\det S_{q\alpha}\neq0$ at the base point, together with the momentum map
$p=S_{q}$ and the Jacobi constants $\beta=S_{\alpha}$.

downstream_pages.affected_use:
**E1 — harmonic reduction and the subsidiary system.** The gauge vector
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$, the reduced Einstein
equation and the constraint residuals are defined in
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Its principal part and
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction are
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]]; smooth initial data with vanishing
initial gauge give a smooth reduced solution in
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]]. The residual identity
$E_{ab}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a-g_{ab}\nabla^cH_c)$ and the
homogeneous wave equation for $H$ are
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]]; the constraint
equations in the normal frame, with the Gauss and Codazzi equations, are
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; and the construction of the
initial metric jet from $(h,K)$ that makes the gauge vanish initially is
[[lem-gr-harmonic-initial-data-construction]]. The propagation theorem
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]] then closes the reduction: a
reduced solution with vanishing initial gauge and constraints solves the full
field equation near the initial surface.
